core_obligations: Write the graded pieces of both cokernels as subquotients of the target (proof lines 263-268).
Prove the inclusion g(M) cap I^n N contained in I^{n+1}N + g'(M) cap I^n N, splitting into the cases n at most c and n larger than c (proof lines 268-281).
Invoke symmetry of the situation to obtain the reverse inclusion and conclude that the graded modules agree (proof lines 281).
proof_roadmap: Express both graded pieces as subquotients (proof lines 263-268).
Prove one inclusion by the valuation computation (proof lines 268-278).
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares the associated graded modules of the two cokernels appearing in the Artin-Rees perturbation statement, and the proof is a 19-line argument that proves one inclusion between the two filtered pieces and then invokes symmetry. The inclusion is checked by writing an element of the intersection as g(a) with a controlled valuation, subtracting the corresponding element for g', and using the hypothesis that the two maps agree modulo the higher power of the ideal. The valuation bookkeeping is where the content lies, and the author displays both the claim and the symmetry argument.
